blocks.text: Why legal billing codes matter for your firm

Correct legal billing codes ensure that clients understand the value of the work performed. When descriptions are vague, partners often write down the time. This hurts your utilization rate. A firm with 20 paralegals loses significant revenue if utilization drops from 90% to 80%. You need to capture every billable minute to meet your annual targets.

Delayed entry is the biggest culprit. If you wait until Friday to log time for Monday, you will forget details. This leads to generic notes like 'reviewed file' instead of 'reviewed medical records for case 12345'. Another issue is multitasking. It is hard to track time when you jump between three different matters in one hour. Use a timer or a dedicated note to keep track of your active matter.
Simple fixes for better billing accuracy

items: Use a dedicated time tracker on your Mac to log tasks as they happen.
Create a list of common legal billing codes for your practice area.
Keep a simple text file open in TextEdit to note down start and end times.
Review your entries before you submit them to the billing partner.
Use keyboard shortcuts to switch between apps faster.

blocks.text: How to use your Mac to stay organized

Your Mac has built in tools to help. Use Mission Control to organize your windows. Keep your case management software in one space and your email in another. Use ⌘ + Tab to switch between them. If you use Outlook, use the Quick Parts feature to insert standard billing descriptions. This saves time and keeps your language consistent.
Always follow your firm's rules regarding client data. Never put sensitive information into public AI tools. Your firm's security policy is the final word.

faq.question: How can I improve my billing speed?
faq.answer: Use templates for common tasks and log your time immediately after finishing a document or call.

faq.question: What if I forget to log time?
faq.answer: Review your sent folder in Outlook or your file history in Word to see what you worked on that day.
